title: Representative normalization of the specified native evaluation tensor isomorphism
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l, a scheme W, a coefficient derived system calculus S [def-coef-derived-system-calculus-data], and a level n. Use the native coefficient sequence site and exact evaluation e_n [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site], and TensorComparisonModel [def-coef-semilinear-system-models]. Then the specified isomorphism S.evaluationTensor(n), between evaluation of the system derived tensor and the finite derived tensor of evaluations, admits a TensorComparisonModel relative to the closed structures and tensor models stored in S. The ordinary comparison of this model is exactly ordinaryEvaluationTensor on every pair of coefficient system module sheaves. No boundedness, flatness, or cartesianness hypothesis is imposed on the pair of module sheaves.

source.place: Tag 07A4, sites-cohomology-lemma-pullback-tensor-product; Tag 0941 sequence-site evaluation; sites-modules.tex Tag 03EK, tensor product of module sheaves. Representative-normalization consequence for the already specified calculus evaluation tensor.

proof.text: Use ordinaryEvaluationTensor for the ordinary model field and the inverse of evaluationTotalIso for the chain field. Its total-summand equation is exactly the summand condition in TensorComparisonModel. Evaluation preserves independently K-flat complexes, so it gives the K-flat model field.

The inverse generator formula for evaluationTotalIso and cancellation of that isomorphism give its forward pure-generator formula. By the uniqueness in coefficientEvaluationTensorIso_exists it equals the native coefficientEvaluationTensorIso; the section transports agree on their underlying carriers.

Substitute that equality into S.evaluationTensor_normalization. Compose with the inverses of the finite tensor model, tensor of factorization isomorphisms, evaluation tensor isomorphism, and evaluated system tensor model. Cancellation gives precisely the derived field of TensorComparisonModel. Assemble these five fields. Their ordinary field was defined to be ordinaryEvaluationTensor, which gives the asserted equality.

theorem coefficientEvaluationTensorModel_exists (W : Scheme.{u})
    (S : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus.{u, u} l E W) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ model : (
      let := coefficientSequenceEvaluation_additiveInstance l E W n
      let := coefficientSequenceEvaluation_limits l E W n
      let := coefficientSequenceEvaluation_colimits l E W n
      @TensorComparisonModel.{u+1, u, u}
        (ℕ × W.ProEt) _ (coefficientSequenceTopology (ProEt.topology W))
        (ProEtale.VaryingRing.sequenceSiteSmall W)
        W.ProEt _ (ProEtale.VaryingRing.siteSmall W) (ProEt.topology W)
        (coefficientSequenceCommRingSheaf l E W) (integralCoefficientCommRingSheaf l E W n)
        (coefficientSequenceEvaluation l E W n)
        (coefficientSequenceEvaluation_additiveInstance l E W n)
        (coefficientSequenceEvaluation_limits l E W n)
        (coefficientSequenceEvaluation_colimits l E W n)
        S.systemClosed (S.finiteClosed n) S.systemTensorModel (S.finiteTensorModel n)
        (S.evaluationTensor n)),
      ∀ M N : coefficientSequenceModules l E W,
        (modelField% ordinary model) M N =
          ordinaryEvaluationTensor.{u+1, u, u} (ProEt.topology W)
            (integralCoefficientCommRingSheaf l E W)
            (coefficientSequenceCommRingTransition l E W) n M N
